Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. ADDED BEYOND THE BOOK: the typical adult value of about 40 to 45 per cent is standard physiology and is not printed in this book's answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What it measures
steps.why: It is a ratio, so the answer must say what is measured against what — cell volume against whole blood volume.
common_mistakes: Writing that it is the number of red blood cells. It is a volume, not a count.
Leaving out the word percentage. The value is a percentage.
steps.memory_tip: Spin the blood: the packed red column, as a percentage of the whole column, is the haematocrit.
steps.margin_note: One sentence of definition. Say percentage, and say volume.

steps.label: Its other name
steps.why: The second name explains the first one: the packed cells are the red cell column left at the bottom after spinning.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the second name. Packed cell volume is the term the examiner looks for.
steps.memory_tip: Packed cell volume names the method: the cells are packed at the bottom of the tube.
steps.margin_note: The second name is the mark. The typical value is a useful extra line.
